source.title: Forgetting That Sticks: Quantization-Permanent Unlearning via Circuit Attribution
source.authors: Saisab Sadhu; Pratinav Seth; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies NF4 post-training quantization to unlearned checkpoints and measures whether targeted-knowledge accuracy returns. This directly tests quantization recovery, but is a different evaluation of the broader reversibility claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own NF4 results and circuit-attribution measurements. The cited 83% recovery result from prior work is not recorded as a row. Fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, and prompt-only recovery are not performed; mentions of them are not results.
record.test_reason: The study applies NF4 4-bit quantization to checkpoints from six existing unlearning methods and reports forget-set accuracy before and after. That is a direct test of quantization recovery (D). It also tests whether baselines reach near-chance forgetting with utility intact (A). CAD analysis of LUNAR bears on C's access-blocking clause. MANSU is a new method evaluated against NF4 (F). None of these papers is an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim a systematic 'dual failure'. Gradient-based methods lose forgetting under NF4. Preference and null-space methods survive only because they barely change the model (mean 1.6 pp forget reduction across 94 runs). They trace both failures to updates below NF4 bin width. MANSU yields non-positive PTQ gaps, preserved MMLU and high CAD. They propose the PTQ gap and CAD as standard evaluation additions. The paper tests quantization only.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces MANSU, combining circuit attribution, circuit-restricted updates, a retain constraint, and an NF4 magnitude floor; it evaluates existing unlearning baselines under NF4 rather than reproducing one original study's complete recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, model, unlearning method, MANSU circuit size k, and floor margin α vary. The paper reports that MANSU performance changes with k and α (Tables 12–13). NF4 is the tested quantizer; GPTQ is not used.

fits_no_version.finding: MANSU's high CAD with low AS-NC is interpreted as localized structural erasure of the forget circuit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit-restricted unlearning dismantles the attributed knowledge circuit rather than redirecting access.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-parameter update RMS for Global GA and Surgical GA is 1/828 and 1/47 of the NF4 bin width (Table 15). The authors propose this as the mechanism of quantization recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization recovery occurs because unlearning updates fall below quantization bin width.

record.code_released: not stated; implementation and evaluation scripts are said to be released upon acceptance. The cited EAP-IG repository is github.com/hannamw/EAP-IG.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the main results. The primary evaluation uses 100 forget questions and 400 MMLU questions. The paper's strict quantization guarantee is scoped to weights in narrow NF4 bins; its implementation uses α = 0.704, and it describes the remaining tail-weight coverage as empirical. Fine-tuning and prompt attacks are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: The full baseline and MANSU sweeps across all models and domains in Tables 2 and 6–9 are not individually enumerated; the main WMDP-bio method comparisons and MANSU cross-domain results are retained here. Other Table 3 CAD conditions, component-ablation outcomes in Tables 4 and 12–13, and the reported aggregate statistics are omitted to keep the catalog focused on the claim versions tested.

untested.parts: No activation-direction ablation and no recovery shown via internal edits. Only CAD attribution analysis.
GPTQ, AWQ, and bit widths other than 4-bit NF4.
MANSU is tested only against NF4, not fine-tuning, ablation or prompting.

record.verdict_notes: Row versions were remapped from V1–V6 to A–F. The text overstates its own numbers. The abstract and introduction say gradient methods recover +0.06 to +0.07, but Table 2 Llama bio shows +0.050 max. Rows left out (declared) contain larger recoveries: Qwen-3-8B cyber SimNPO +0.133 and GU+SimNPO +0.110 (Table 2), and Global GA cyber +0.233 in Table 8. That cell conflicts with Table 2 (+0.017 for the same model, method and domain), an internal inconsistency. These larger cells would strengthen D in some settings. Other limits: no uncertainty is reported; the forget set is 100 questions, so ±0.02 is 2 questions; MANSU's best checkpoint was chosen on forget accuracy using the evaluation indices. The authors concede the C-relevant LUNAR CAD result holds by construction.

versions.untested_parts: No tests of fine-tuning or prompt-based attacks. The paper tests NF4 recovery, but not every simple attack named in the claim.
No small-set fine-tuning or relearning attack is performed.
No activation-direction ablation is performed. The paper uses circuit attribution and activation-shift measures to assess whether changes appear structural or redirected.
Tests NF4 post-training quantization; GPTQ and AWQ are not tested.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack is performed.
MANSU is evaluated against NF4 quantization only, not fine-tuning, internal-direction ablation, or prompting attacks.
